messages:
Anya (PM): Quick sync — I pushed a first-pass PRD for 'commit window sizing & degradation matrix' for Dedicated capacity. Link: https://rwd.internal/prd/commit-window-dgm :point_right: Please read and drop acceptance criteria + risky edge cases by EOD.
Dave (SRE): reading now. main ask: what's the target latency SLO under commit constraints? P99 tail behavior matters for customers.
Anya (PM): thinking `commit_window_slo = 99.5%` for 1s token latency under normal load, degrade gracefully under <50% reserved capacity. Open to suggestions.
Kevin (Eng-Platform): we should be explicit about throughput vs slot allocation. If a tenant has 10 reserved slots, is burst allowed to 20 for short windows? need matrix: steady / burst / coldstart.
Marta (Product): Customers asked for predictable throughput for B2B plans — they want hard guarantees during business hours, and cheaper burst at night. We should include time-based commit windows in the PRD.
Dave (SRE): agree on time-based windows. Also propose a degradation matrix like:

```
State        | Allowed QPS per slot | Latency target
-------------|-----------------------|---------------
Normal       | 1.0x                 | P50 < 100ms, P95 < 300ms, P99 < 1s
Burst (30s)  | 2.0x                 | P50 < 200ms, P95 < 600ms, P99 < 2s
Coldstart    | 0.5x (no warmpool)   | P50 < 400ms, P95 < 1s, P99 < 3s
Degraded     | fallback to smaller  | best-effort
```

We need to define exact time thresholds, warmpool sizes, and rollout behavior.
Kevin (Eng-Platform): For autoscale rules: suggest `scale_up_threshold = 85%` sustained for 15s, `scale_down_threshold = 30%` sustained for 120s. Warmpool target = min(2, floor(commit_slots*0.1)). That gives at least 2 warm workers for small commits.
Anya (PM): Good. Add acceptance criteria to PRD: 1) canary shows <10% error increase vs baseline, 2) degradation follows matrix within 2x latency for P95, 3) no coldpath OOMs in 5k request burst test.
Marta (Product): Add customer-impact test: simulate reserved tenant traffic + cross-tenant noisy neighbor to verify isolation.
Dave (SRE): Edge cases I want documented:
- sudden N+1 tenant warmup causing transient throttling
- queued requests hitting request TTL during scale-up
- model-variant fallback (quantized -> full) and token accounting differences

Kevin (Eng-Platform): Operational knobs in PRD: `burst_budget`, `commit_window_seconds`, `warmpool_size`, `fallback_model_rank`. Need default values and per-tenant overrides.
Anya (PM): For rollout plan: start with 5 internal tenants, then 10 early-access customers, then gradual ramp to GA. Canary metrics: error budget usage, P95 delta, slot utilization.
infra-bot: Deploy preview posted: https://rwd.ci/build/3821 — canary config under `prd/commit-window/canary-v1.yaml`
Marta (Product): Prioritization note: if we can't hit 99.5% P99 in initial ship, we should ship with limited GA and document known degradations. Customers prefer transparency.
Dave (SRE): Tests to add to the acceptance suite:
- burst storm: 100 tenants, random bursts, measure tail latencies
- warmpool eviction: simulate node failures and ensure fallback slots bring up within 45s
- cross-region fallback: ensure routing policy falls back to compatible region within 2s

Kevin (Eng-Platform): Small nit: define what counts toward reserved capacity for multi-model routes (few customers will pin multiple heavy models).
Anya (PM): I'll update PRD with all of the above. Action items:
- @Kevin: add exact autoscale YAML and default values (due tomorrow)
- @Dave: add SRE test matrix and scripts (due EOD Fri)
- @Marta: collect top 3 customer asks to anchor degradation priorities (due Tue)
- @infra-bot: attach canary logs after each run :robot_face:

Marta (Product): :thumbsup: I'll also add a short note on commercial constraints (commit window billing implications) so we can align pricing with guarantees.
Dave (SRE): Quick question — for the degradation fallback, do we prefer graceful token-dropping or 429s? My inclination: prefer soft degradation (partial responses) for non-critical flows.
Anya (PM): We'll document both modes: `soft_degrade` (partial/resumable output) and `hard_reject` (429) per route. Default: soft for chat/generation, hard for transactional APIs.
Kevin (Eng-Platform): OK. I'll prototype a `degradation_policy` schema and push a RFC snippet.
Anya (PM): Thanks everyone. Please leave any quick comments here. If no major objections by EOD, I'll mark PRD ready for RFC review.
Marta (Product): No blockers from product side. minor wording edits incoming.
Dave (SRE): lgtm apart from OOM test detail, I'll post specifics.
infra-bot: Canary run completed: build 3821 — metrics posted: https://rwd.ci/artifacts/3821/metrics.json :white_check_mark:
Anya (PM): Sweet — I'll iterate the PRD now and tag for RFC. :rocket:
